coaching.title: Hills 6mi + 1,200ft — Descending Focus
coaching.message: Peak phase, 43 days out. Today is your Week 2 vert build: 6 miles with ~1,200 ft of gain. Climb steady at Zone 2 to low Zone 3 (heart rate roughly 132–155 bpm) and power hike anything steep — hiking strong is a race skill, not a concession. The real work is the descent: run down with control, quick light feet, and a slight forward lean to load the quads eccentrically. That downhill durability is exactly what Julian Alps' ~2,500m of alpine descent will demand. Go at first light to beat the San Salvador heat and run effort, not pace.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Short and hilly, but train the gut anyway. Top off with 30–40g easy carbs 30–45 min pre-run (banana or toast + honey). In the heat, sodium is the priority: 600–800mg per hour via electrolyte drink. If you take the full hour, sip 40–60g carbs/hr. Then hit the recovery window within 30 min — 25–30g protein plus carbs (target the 3:1 carb-to-protein range) to rebuild after all that eccentric descending.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Descending trashes the quads with micro-damage, so get ahead of the DOMS. Do 10 min of easy spin or a walk to flush the legs, then foam roll quads, calves, and glutes tonight. Elevate the legs for a few minutes and prioritize protein at dinner. Expect some quad soreness tomorrow — that's the adaptation you want. Aim for 7.5–8+ hours of sleep.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: In the Alps, races are won and lost on the downhills — most runners brake, tense up, and shred their legs. Use every descent today as a rehearsal: relax the shoulders, trust your feet, let gravity work for you. You're building a superpower most of the field won't have. Six weeks out, every controlled descent is a deposit you'll cash on September 18.
